Goodbye Sandton

By: Sibusisiwe Buthelezi | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We expose a syndicate behind the decay of Sandton.

Unique Selling Point:
We will have two confrontations.

Summary:
We are constantly told property is the best investment because the value appreciates over the years. But what happens to the value of property when squatters move into the neighborhood? Or worse, what happens when a property syndicate hijacks your home?

This is what is happening in Bryanston and many other neighborhoods across Sandton. According to the City of Joburg, in Bryanston alone, 17 houses have been hijacked while at least 21 houses have been hijacked in Buccleuch.

The syndicate targets homes of owners who live abroad or mostly travel for work.

We will focus on exposing the property syndicate because it is important to inform South Africans as well as prevent them from taking over more homes.

The city is owed millions in debt for electricity, yet all of these properties seem to have electricity that has been connected illegally. So that means not only are they stealing from the homeowner but they are also stealing from the city and the taxpayers.
Some of the houses also have free access to water, while the rest of South Africans have to pay for water.

Press Release:


They’re multimillion-rand properties in prime locations. But behind high walls, syndicates are moving in. In Johannesburg's luxury suburbs, property syndicates target absentee owners and hijack under-protected homes, subletting to hundreds of residents, making illegal electricity and water connections, and leaving a trail of makeshift structures and destruction. Desperate homeowners wait years for the City to evict squatters, while neighbours suffer crime and nosediving property values. Who is behind a rise in home hijackings and why is the City dragging its feet? Carte Blanche investigates.

Script:


(Alex Babich)- It’s good to see you, Alex, hi.
(Govan)- I’m Govan.
(Govan)- We are in Bryanston, in Johannesburg’s northern suburbs.
(Govan)- We’ve been called to this house by concerned residents, Lynda Shackleford and Alex Babich.
(Govan)- Can’t see much from here. Can we open it?
(Alex Babich)- Got it.
(Govan)- Oh wow, what? What? Look at this, how much would you say this property’s worth?
(Alex Babich)- You’ve got a call it R8 million to R10 million property, that’s your bedroom and you’re overlooking this.
(Govan)- Let’s see if it looks the same inside.
(Govan)- This is a room that has become a braai room, come look at this.
(Alex Babich)- This is where they cook at night, bottles everywhere.
(Govan)- It feels like we’re invading someone’s privacy but this is a hijacked house in the middle of Bryanston. One of the most up market neighborhoods in Johannesburg.
(Govan)- You know you can’t live for free?
(Squatter) Hmm.
(Govan)- Why are you doing this?
(Alex Babich)- Remember there's also people masquerading in suits, you're just seeing the lower pecking order here.
(Govan)- Lynda, who is also the ward councillor here, says the community is deeply frustrated: this house isn’t an isolated case.
(Govan)- Many of these properties have been bought by developers who are waiting for municipal approval to start building.
(Lynda Shackleford)- The property sits abandoned. They leave a gentleman on the property and he takes the initiative and starts to rent out space in that house.
(Govan)- This owner lives just down the road - yet he’s just as helpless. Six kilometres away in Wendywood is the house that Kapiel Naidoo bought, three years ago.
(Govan)- Did you buy the property from an owner?
(Kapiel Naidoo)- We bought the property from the bank via a repossession auction and the owner was still residing in the property and still refusing to leave the property.
(Govan)- At first Kapiel tried to resolve the matter amicably.
(Kapiel Naidoo)- We even offered him to move out and we were prepared to pay him a certain amount.
(Govan)- Instead of moving out, the previous owner, Moses Reeds, built illegal structures on the property, and rented them out.
(Govan)- The utilities bill - in Kapiel’s name - is R450 000, while Reeds and his tenants allegedly enjoy free water and electricity. Worse still, Kapiel still has to pay the bank R13 000 every month.
Kapiel Naidoo)- If you stop the payment then your credit record gets impaired and we won’t be able to be good borrowers anymore.
(Govan)- You can’t give back the house?
Kapiel Naidoo)- No we can’t give back the house.
(Govan)- Fed up, Kapiel approached the court for an eviction order, which was granted in January 2024. But two years and R200 000 in legal fees later, he has still not been able to set foot inside his house.

Kapiel Naidoo)- It’s been very difficult to understand initially as to why we have to go through all of this and the costs, and the time, when there’s someone who clearly is breaking the law.
(Govan)- The Prevention of Illegal Eviction and Unlawful Occupation of Land Act (PIE) is intended to protect vulnerable tenants from unscrupulous landlords.
(Govan)- But Kapiel says it’s created a monster because occupants will not move out until they have alternative accommodation.
Kapiel Naidoo)- It seems as though homeowners do not enjoy the protection of the court as opposed to the people who are illegally occupying.
(Govan)- And the City, which is tasked with enforcing the law, seems to be overwhelmed.
(Govan)- City of Joburg has a unit dedicated to dealing with hijacked properties but that unit has been accused of dragging its feet. So what’s the hold up?
(Govan)- We were initially granted an interview with the head of the unit.
(Govan)- But once we had set up our cameras, plans changed.
(Govan)- Nthatisi let’s begin by explaining why you’re doing the interview and not the head of the anti-hijacking unit?
(Nthatisi Modingoane)- I am the official spokesperson of the City of Johannesburg and I should understand all the operations of all the departments.
(Govan)- It soon becomes apparent, that statement may not be true.
(Govan)- Do you know how many hijacked properties you’ve saved?
(Nthatisi Modingoane)- Uhm that number would be a ball park figure because-
(Govan)- It shouldn’t be because the unit keeps records.
(Nthatisi Modingoane)- Ya. Uhm, I need to check that number.
(Govan)- In fact, Modingoane isn’t even sure how many Joburg properties have been hijacked.
(Govan)- Do you know if the numbers are rising?
(Nthatisi Modingoane)- At the moment I’m not sure if they are rising.
(Govan)- The properties under investigation are divided into two categories, problem properties and hijacked properties.
(Govan)- What makes a property problematic?
(Nthatisi Modingoane)- When one, you start seeing grime happening. There’s disregard of regulations in terms of upkeeping of the property.
(Nthatisi Modingoane)- Two, the property does not give back revenue to the city. You start seeing the bill exploding to such an extent that though there is no money that is coming… but the services are being consumed in that property.
(Govan)- Modingoane says the unit has 44 active cases in the Sandton area - including both “problem” and hijacked properties.
(Nthatisi Modingoane)- You can’t conclude hijacking before you do the actual active investigation.
(Govan)- That’s why I’m asking how many properties have you established have been hijacked?
(Nthatisi Modingoane)- So far in that part of town, we dealt with two properties.
(Nthatisi Modingoane)- We have a sense of about 17 that we are actively looking into and all the indications are that there might be hijacking happening there.
(Emi Koekemoer)- When you have a hijacking unit that is only capable of doing like two raids a day then it takes them about roughly a week, two weeks to plan that, at that rate you’re never going to make a dent.
(Govan)- Ward councillor Emi Koekemoer is showing us around a problem property in Ferndale.
(Emi Koekemoer)- The owner knows it’s happening now but he’s not doing anything about it. He appointed someone to look after the property.
(Govan)- And that person?
(Emi Koekemoer)- And that person is collecting rent.
(Govan)- The owner, Sifiso Magwaza, confirms that he’s fully aware of the occupants on his property, but says he’s still raising funds to develop it.
(Govan)- How many houses like this exist in Ferndale?
(Emi Koekemoer)- Our current database was standing at roughly about 32 and I can tell you, in the time that this started getting media traction, I’ve received probably 19 tip offs.
(Govan)- That media attention has centred on Bryanston, where the City recently conducted raids on two properties. In one case, the owner has been fighting hijackers for five years.
(News Reporter)- JMPD has arrested a suspect linked to a hijacked mansion in Bryanston.
(Govan)- Lawrence Ramalwa was revealed as the alleged hijacker of both properties and was arrested on the spot.
(Govan)- Through his lawyer, Ramalwa told the court that he is the rightful owner.
(Govan)- He was later released on R1000 bail.
(Govan)- But according to ward councillors, at least 28 other properties remain in the hands of faceless hijackers.
(Govan)- We’re in Wendywood now and we’re going to Kapiel Naidoo’s house. The one that he hasn’t been able to occupy since he bought it. Let’s go speak to Moses Reeds.
(Govan)- How’s it, is it Moses? My name is Govan Whittles, I’m from Carte Blanche. Can I talk to you for a second?
(Moses Reeds)- You can’t do that without asking my permission first for this.
(Govan)- Why do you continue living here when it’s not your house?
(Govan)- Do you have tenants living here? Please come talk to us sir.
(Govan)- After a few minutes, we see him drive out.
(Govan)- Moses why you’re not paying your COJ bills? 09:53:43:34 Moses, are you hijacking this house? Have you hijacked this property?
(Govan)- With the next court appearance set for September, Kapiel has no option but to wait. But the experience has cost him - and not just financially.
(Kapiel Naidoo)- Your kids see the property and they think they’re gonna move into a home with a pool and a big yard etc. And just the fact that you cannot even deliver that, and its no fault of yours, emotionally that creates a massive toll on you.
